description:

No refs/dolt/* exists on origin, so bd dolt push has never run; the same is true for Aurora, RockyRoad and RockyRoadImport, which sync through the git-tracked export instead (Aurora AGENTS.md: 'Sync rides git, not the Dolt remote (unused here)').

title: V6 Branch review page: new, changed, unchanged, removed fixtures against a base ref
description: Replaces the A/B idea. A script takes a base ref (default: merge-base with main), checks it out into a temp git worktree, copies the branch's fixtures in (fixtures that fail to build there are New), screenshots every fixture on both sides with a headless browser (Playwright, Apache-2.0, dev-only), and pixel-diffs them into New, Changed, Unchanged and Removed. It writes a static review page: token diff from V3 at the top, New fixtures shown alone, Changed shown before and after with a toggle and diff highlight, Unchanged collapsed, each linking to the live Cosmos fixture.
acceptance_criteria: Run against main on feat/AuroraGraphTweaks: Select open states are Changed; Popover, Menu, Dialog and Button sm/icon are New; other fixtures are Unchanged. Grille-uoq can be signed off from the page.
notes: Known gap: screenshots capture only the state a fixture renders on load, so hover (and any other interaction-driven state) is not covered. A changed :hover style reads as Unchanged. Workarounds: a fixture that forces the state, or check the live link by hand. Possible follow-up: let a fixture declare an interaction (hover/focus a selector) before the screenshot.
close_reason: scripts/branch-review.mjs (npm run review) builds the review page; verified against main

title: MenuItem: a row tooltip that shows on keyboard focus without a nested tab stop, optionally only when the label is cut off
description:
Rescoped 2026-11-12 after Aurora revisited its assumptions (Aurora-u68h.4, GraphEditorCleanup.md Decisions (owner, refused saves and unsaved marks, 2026-11-12)). Aurora no longer needs a visible description line: it keeps reasons and problem counts out of menus entirely. Saves are never disabled for problems (React Aria's Menu skips disabled items on arrow keys, so a disabled item's reason never reaches a keyboard user); a refused save points at Aurora's own problems chip instead. Unsaved changes show as a dot Aurora draws inside the item, with MenuItem description as screen-reader text.

What remains: Aurora's Open > submenu cuts long effect titles off with an ellipsis (30ch) and must show the full title. Today it wraps the title in its Hint (Grille TooltipTrigger + React Aria Focusable), which puts a focusable element inside the menuitem: React Aria warns in dev, the row gains a nested tab stop, and the tooltip shows on hover only, never when the row is reached with the arrow keys. Give MenuItem and SubmenuItem a tooltip prop that opens after a hover delay and on keyboard focus of the row itself, on Grille's Tooltip skin, with no extra focusable element, plus tooltipOnlyWhenTruncated so it shows only when the label is actually cut off (Aurora drops its 24-character guess). On a submenu row the tooltip is hidden while the flyout is open. Also remove the native title= from menu items: Aurora dropped title= everywhere (w6zq.8), and it neither shows on keyboard focus nor matches the popup skin. MenuItem description stays screen-reader text.

Not needed by Aurora (Grille's call whether to keep for other consumers): descriptionDisplay=line (already removed on the branch), warning on MenuItem/SubmenuItem, warnings on submenu rows, a 'blocked but focusable' disabled item, and click-to-show on disabled rows.

Aurora's intended use on Open > items: tooltip={title} tooltipOnlyWhenTruncated description='Unsaved changes' (only on items with a kept copy). With the branch's precedence (tooltip, then warning, then description) the explicit tooltip wins, so the description is never shown visually there. Document that a row with only a description shows it as a tooltip, or make that opt-in; either works for Aurora as long as it is deliberate.
acceptance_criteria: MenuItem and SubmenuItem take tooltip and tooltipOnlyWhenTruncated: the tooltip opens on hover and on keyboard focus of the row, with no nested focusable and no React Aria warning, only when the label is cut off if asked, and is hidden on a submenu row while its flyout is open; no native title= on menu items; description stays screen-reader text, and whether it alone produces a tooltip is documented; Popup fixtures show a truncated and a fitting row; ui tests cover them; CHANGELOG entry; released in the next 0.1.0-dev.*.
notes:
2026-11-12 (Aurora owner, via the Aurora session): rescoped as above, answering the five questions from the Grille-cou review. 1) Graph problems live only in Aurora's toolbar chip and its popover, not in the menu. 2) Save and Save and apply stay enabled; chosen with problems they show a callout on the chip ('Couldn't save. Fix N problems first.') and then ping the chip; keyboard users get focus on the chip. 3) An effect's unsaved state is a dot on items inside Open > (and on the editor title), never on the Open row; no problem counts. 4) Rewritten on the Aurora side: Aurora-u68h.4, u68h.2, u68h epic, u68h.1 mock (#s6-apply, #s6-menu, #s6-openpath), GraphEditorCleanup.md. 5) Aurora needs only tooltip + tooltipOnlyWhenTruncated, and no title=. The branch's warning prop and click-to-show on disabled rows are not needed by Aurora. Aurora's first consumer is 6d's long-title swap; 6d itself no longer waits on this release.
2026-11-12 (Grille, after rescope): branch trimmed to tooltip + tooltipOnlyWhenTruncated. Removed warning prop + CSS, click-to-show on disabled rows, descriptionDisplay fixtures/tests, the A/B mock fixture. Decision: tooltip is opt-in; description alone is screen-reader text and never shows a tooltip (README + CHANGELOG say so). Hover uses React Aria isHovered (400 ms, matching TooltipTrigger); keyboard focus opens at once. Remaining: browser check in Cosmos ('Menu row tooltips'), log entry, release as next 0.1.0-dev.*.

title: SubmenuItem: maxHeight prop with a default cap and Menu sections with sticky headings, so long grouped submenus scroll
description:
Aurora's graph editor title menu (Aurora-iryq) is getting an Open ▸ submenu that lists every effect in the library, grouped Custom then Built-in (Aurora-u68h.4 later adds a Not saved yet group), so it grows with the user's library. In v0.1.0-dev.10 SubmenuItem renders a hardcoded <Popover className="ui-popover" data-submenu> around <Menu className="ui-menu">, SubmenuItemProps has no way to reach either (id, isDisabled, description, label, aria-label, onAction, children), and ui.css sets no max-height or overflow on .ui-popover or .ui-menu (only .ui-listbox caps at 240px). A long submenu runs off the screen, and Aurora could only fix it by targeting Grille internals. Menu also has no section/heading component, so the groups cannot be labelled.

Reference: Aurora's Dashboard Effects dropdown already does this by hand for the same list (Aurora repo web/ui/EffectPanel.js and web/ui/styles/effect-panel.css, .ef-panel/.ef-scroll/.ef-group): panel capped at min(480px, 100vh - 150px), the list scrolls inside it with overflow-y: auto and overscroll-behavior: contain, group headings are position: sticky; top: 0 on the surface background, and scroll-padding-top: 32px keeps a keyboard-focused row from scrolling under a sticky heading. Match that behaviour so Open ▸ reads like the Dashboard's picker.

1. maxHeight on SubmenuItem: optional, number in px or a CSS length, applied to the submenu so its items scroll inside the popup skin. Default cap without the prop: a token (e.g. --ui-size-submenu-max-height) of 480px, matching the Effects dropdown, and never taller than the space React Aria's Popover leaves on screen. Scroll on the inner menu, not the popover, so the popover padding that keeps the 4px focus ring inside the clip still works; overscroll-behavior: contain so the page does not scroll past the end. Check the default against Aurora's Add node cascade (the other SubmenuItem user): its longest group should not start scrolling unexpectedly.
2. MenuSection with a heading: wrap React Aria's MenuSection + Header as a Grille MenuSection (title prop or Header child), usable in Menu and in a SubmenuItem's children, with the heading styled like a group label (small, secondary text). In a scrolling menu the heading is sticky at the top on the popup background, and the menu has scroll-padding-top equal to the heading height so arrow-key focus never lands hidden under it. Headings are not focusable and are announced as the group label.
acceptance_criteria: SubmenuItem accepts maxHeight; with no prop, a submenu longer than the 480px default (or the space on screen) scrolls inside the popup, and short submenus are unchanged; the focus ring is not clipped; arrow-key navigation scrolls the focused item into view and never under a sticky heading; MenuSection renders a heading that is sticky while scrolling, is skipped by the keyboard and labels its group for screen readers; Aurora's Add node cascade is unaffected; a Popup fixture shows a long grouped submenu; ui tests cover maxHeight, the default and MenuSection; CHANGELOG entry; released in the next 0.1.0-dev.* so Aurora-iryq can bump to it.

title: Dropdown triggers flip their chevron while the popup is open

Select gets it for free.

title: Popover: clicking the trigger of an open non-modal popover closes it, then the click reopens it
description: React Aria's usePopover sets shouldCloseOnBlur: true. Pressing the trigger moves focus to it (Chrome; Safari does not focus buttons on click), so the popover closes on blur, then the trigger's onClick toggle sees open=false and reopens it. Every Aurora editor menu (Add node, View, title, Test caret) shows it. Fix in Grille's Popover: ignore the blur close when focus moves into triggerRef, so the trigger's own toggle is the only closer.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking the trigger of an open isNonModal Popover leaves it closed (test plus a Cosmos fixture); Tab out of the popover still closes it; focus restore unchanged.

title: Icons for Aurora and RockyRoad
description:
Aurora's graph editor draws icons from three places: SVG files in Aurora's web/ui/icons, Unicode glyphs that render per OS font, and Grille's own glyphs (Drawer close ×, Select ▾). Aurora's icon audit (Aurora-daaa.33, table in Aurora web/graph-editor/README.md 'Icon audit') settled the set: Vidstack media-icons (MIT) where it has the shape, Zest Free for undo, redo and minus, and Aurora's own warning mark. Grille should own one icon set that React and non-React consumers both use.

Approach (agreed in Aurora, 2026-11-11): vendor path data into Grille rather than depend on an icon package. @vidstack/react/icons is part of the full player package (pulls media-captions and @floating-ui/dom); the npm zest-icons 0.0.6 depends on React 16 and styled-components; scripts/check-ui-boundary.mjs allows only react, react-dom, react-aria-components and @fontsource/inter in src. One source builds both a React component and plain SVG for pages without React (Aurora's Dashboard is plain JS using mountIsland; static mocks copy ui.css only).

title: Seed docs/lessons/ with generalized Grille lessons from Aurora, RockyRoad and RockyRoadImport

Proposed files: components.md (focus, ARIA, popups, events), css-tokens.md (cascade, layers, tokens), packaging-release.md (licenses, fonts, consumer contract), plus engineering-hygiene.md if general ones are adopted. Each entry: ## principle headline, Tags:, Applies-when:, root cause, **Fix:**, and an origin line naming the source repo + headline. Candidates:
- Aurora components.md: Drawer focus/Esc vs document-level key listeners; React Aria popups on a host that captures pointer/keyboard; disabling the focused control drops focus; ARIA commit-on-every-interaction; option values assumed to be strings.
- Aurora webui-testing.md: getByRole misses react-aria submenus (SubmenuItem).
- Aurora build-toolchain.md: Vite license output omits CSS-referenced fonts (Inter).
- Aurora layout-css.md: focus rings from shared tokens + one :focus-visible rule; scoped reset in a later stylesheet needs :where().
- RockyRoad desktop-dom.md: popover stopPropagation; shared .btn base vs earlier screen rules; child-combinator vs insertion point.
- RockyRoadImport: tests + clean build don't prove correctness against real content; generated export is the recovery path; upstream-dependencies entries restated from the library side (upstream fix changing behavior a consumer patch got right; keep the guess in the consumer).
Aurora originals stay in place.

title: Drawer: a non-modal side panel for Aurora's graph editor stage 4

design:
Behavior: non-modal, no scrim, the rest of the page stays usable with the drawer open (the user keeps wiring and selecting on the canvas). Controlled isOpen/onOpenChange. Closes on Escape while focus is inside, and on its close button; an outside click does NOT close it. Focus moves into the drawer on open and returns to the opener on close (same focus-restore approach as the G3a popups). One open at a time is the consumer's job, not Grille's.
Semantics: a labelled region with a heading (title), optional subtitle, and a scrolling body; not role=dialog aria-modal. Close button labelled 'Close'.
Layout: fixed to one edge (right by default), top offset settable so it sits below an app bar, full remaining height, width a token. Overlays the content, does not push it. Aurora popup skin from G2 (surface, border, shadow token that can be none for WebXR). Body scroll keeps the focus ring unclipped (4px padding or the inset ring, per the Aurora-t2hz finding).
Reference: web/ui/Static_GraphEditor_Mocks/mock.js drawer() in the Aurora repo.
acceptance_criteria: Drawer exported with a fixture that passes the guard test; tests cover open/close, Escape, outside click leaving it open, focus in on open and back to the opener on close, and that the page behind stays interactive; released as the next v0.1.0-dev.N prerelease.

title: Drawer: bottom side with a half/full toggle (non-modal, narrow windows)
description: Aurora's graph editor docks its drawers (node Details, Dashboard controls) at the bottom when the window is narrow (below about 650 px) or clearly portrait, because a 280-350 px side drawer then covers most of the canvas. Drawer today takes side: 'right' | 'left' only. Decided in Aurora docs/planning/WebUI/GraphEditorCleanup.md, Decisions (narrow windows). Aurora's consumer copy is Aurora-daaa.29.3. Follow-up to Grille-vxt; could ship in the same prerelease as Grille-g25.
design: side: 'bottom' anchors to the bottom edge, full width, border on top. Opens at half the space below 'top'; a visible toggle button in the head switches half/full (aria-expanded, label Expand / Collapse), so the size change is reachable by keyboard and understandable without a gesture. Still non-modal: no scrim, the surface above stays usable. Same focus, Esc and close-button behaviour as the side variants. Optional controlled props (expanded, onExpandedChange) so a host can pan its canvas when the height changes. No drag handle and no free resize in this pass (later, as a WAI-ARIA window splitter, only if asked). Height token alongside --ui-size-drawer-width.
acceptance_criteria: Drawer accepts side='bottom' and renders half height by default; the toggle switches to full and back and reports aria-expanded; Esc and close behave as on the right side; the right and left variants are unchanged; a Cosmos fixture shows the bottom drawer over a surface that stays clickable; published in a new dev prerelease.

title: Drawer: close on Esc when focus is outside it (non-modal use)
description: Drawer (v0.1.0-dev.7) handles Esc through an onKeyDown on its own section, so Esc closes it only while focus is inside. Aurora's graph editor uses it non-modally: it stays open on canvas clicks so wiring can continue, which leaves focus on the canvas, and Esc then does nothing. The stage 4 decision says the drawer is closed by Esc or its close button. Found in Aurora-daaa.27.3: open drawer, click canvas, press Esc, drawer stays. Follow-up to Grille-vxt. Aurora has a workaround, so nothing is blocked. Aurora's copy of this issue is Aurora-daaa.27.5.
design:
Option A: Drawer adds a window keydown listener while open, closing on Escape unless e.defaultPrevented or a menu, popover or dialog is open. Pro: every non-modal use gets it, and Aurora's workaround goes away. Con: Drawer now knows about other overlays, and a page with several Esc handlers must cooperate. Option B: keep as is and document that a non-modal host owns Esc when focus is outside. Pro: no coupling. Con: every consumer re-implements the guard. Option C: opt-in prop (e.g. closeOnEscapeAnywhere) so a modal-style drawer keeps today's behaviour. Leaning A or C. Either way, Esc inside a nested menu must close only the menu first, then the drawer on the next Esc.

Aurora's workaround (web/graph-editor/src/App.tsx): window keydown for Escape while a drawer is open; skip if e.defaultPrevented or document.querySelector('.react-aria-Popover, [role="menu"], [role="dialog"]') matches; else close. Browser-verified: with a menu open and focus outside the drawer, the first Esc closes the menu and the drawer stays; the second closes the drawer; Esc inside the drawer still closes it. The selector is a DOM probe and could miss a popup type Grille adds later, which is the argument for fixing it in Grille.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded (A, B or C). If A or C: Drawer tests cover Esc with focus outside and with a menu open over it; new dev prerelease cut.
notes: Decision: Option A. Drawer adds a window keydown listener while open; skips if defaultPrevented or a .ui-popover/.ui-modal-overlay/[role=menu]/[role=dialog] is in the DOM. Tests cover focus outside and a menu open over it. Version 0.1.0-dev.8.
